Title: Can't use AjaxResponse with success = true when passed result is Boolean
Description: i need to convert the result to object before passing it to AjaxResponse
`return new AjaxResponse((object)isUnique);`

if i didn't convert to object it will call the override method which take success or failure as input and return response with result : null

llm_response:
I'll analyze this GitHub issue to determine if a build environment is needed to verify the solution.

CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue is about a specific behavior of the AjaxResponse class where passing a Boolean value directly causes it to use an overloaded constructor that treats the Boolean as a success/failure flag rather than as the result data. The solution is to cast the Boolean to object before passing it to AjaxResponse: `return new AjaxResponse((object)isUnique);`. 

This is a straightforward code issue that can be verified through code analysis without needing to build or run the application. The problem is related to method overloading in C# where the compiler chooses the wrong overload when a Boolean is passed directly. The solution (casting to object) forces the compiler to use the correct constructor overload.

An LLM can verify this solution is correct by understanding C# method resolution rules and how casting affects which overloaded method gets called. No build environment is necessary to confirm this behavior or the effectiveness of the solution.
